title_en: MacroVoices #554 Dr. Anas Alhajji + Louis-Vincent Gave: Developing Crises in Middle-East and France
title_zh: MacroVoices #554 Anas Alhajji 与 Louis-Vincent Gave：中东与法国酝酿中的危机
subtitle_zh: 能源经济学家 Anas Alhajji 解析霍尔木兹、红海、黑海「三海危机」对全球能源与炼化的冲击，Gavekal 的 Louis-Vincent Gave 剖析法国财政与政治乱局及欧元风险，交易台 Patrick Ceresna 给出多空配对与市场脉搏。

speakers.4: Patrick Ceresna（Big Picture Trading，市场交易台）

turns.en: And when we talk about the crisis, we are talking about the Gulf, we are talking about the Red Sea, and we are also talking about the Black Sea. This has changed energy markets forever. That was Energy Outlook Advisor's founder, Dr. Anasal Haji. I'm Eric Townsend, and this is Mack Roe Voices, the free weekly podcast targeting professional
turns.zh: 当我们谈论这场危机时，我们说的是波斯湾（the Gulf）、红海（Red Sea），还有黑海（Black Sea）。它已经永远地改变了能源市场。刚才那段话，出自 Energy Outlook Advisor 的创始人 Anas Alhajji 博士。我是 Erik Townsend，这里是 Macro Voices——一档面向专业

turns.en: finance and sophisticated private investors. Episode 555 was produced on October 22nd, 2026. With some popcorn folks, with crises in both the Middle East and France mushrooming this week, we decided to cover both, and that will make for a very long episode.
turns.zh: 金融人士和成熟私人投资者的一周免费播客。本期是第 554 集，制作于 2026 年 10 月 22 日。各位准备好爆米花——中东和法国两地的危机本周都在迅速发酵，我们决定两个都聊，所以这一集会非常长。

turns.en: But I think you'll find the content in both of our double header feature interviews to be very worthwhile. Our scheduled feature interview guest is Dr. Anasal Haji, and the subject is the rapidly developing geopolitical situation and its impact on global energy markets.
turns.zh: 但我相信，你们会觉得今天这两场“连打”重磅访谈的内容都非常值得。我们预定的重磅访谈嘉宾是 Anas Alhajji 博士，主题是迅速演变的地缘政治局势，以及它对全球能源市场的影响。

turns.en: And I will discuss the energy week conferences that he just attended in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, what he learned there, and the rapidly escalating refining capacity crisis that I think could threaten global energy security for many years after the wars have ended.
turns.zh: 我会和他聊聊他刚在沙特阿拉伯利雅得（Riyadh）参加的能源周（Energy Week）系列会议、他从中了解到的情况，以及正在迅速升级的炼油产能危机——我认为，即便战争结束，这场危机在此后很多年里都可能威胁全球能源安全。

turns.en: Finally, we'll discuss Vladimir Putin's proposal for a summit with President Trump and Xi Jinping, which apparently, for a lot of years, Zelensky would not be invited to. I know many of you have been looking forward to a macro voices unplugged long form bonus session with Dr. Anas, and I'm really looking forward to that one myself.
turns.zh: 最后，我们会讨论 Vladimir Putin 提出的、与 Trump 总统和习近平（Xi Jinping）举行峰会的提议——而且显然 Zelensky 不会被邀请参加。我知道你们中有很多人一直期待着一期与 Anas 博士的 Macro Voices Unplugged 长谈加更节目，我自己也非常期待。

turns.en: But unfortunately, due to Anas's numerous commitments to other public speaking obligations, as well as my own suffering from bronchitis that you can probably tell from my voice, we were unable to commit to the time needed to pull that one together for you this week.
turns.zh: 但很不巧，一方面 Anas 有很多其他公开演讲的安排，另一方面我自己得了支气管炎（bronchitis）——你们从我的嗓音大概能听出来——所以我们这周实在腾不出足够的时间把那期节目做出来给你们。

turns.en: We promise to bring that episode to you the next time that we bring Anas back for another feature interview. We're going to make it up to you this week, though, by adding a special cameo appearance in this episode by Gav Cal, founder and CEO, Louis Vincent Gav.
turns.zh: 我们保证，下次请 Anas 回来做重磅访谈时，一定把那期节目补上。不过这一周我们会弥补一下——本期特别加入了 Gavekal 创始人兼 CEO Louis-Vincent Gave 的客串亮相。

turns.en: Louis and I will discuss the rapidly devolving situation in France, what's driving it, and what it means for traders, will also tie it into the energy crisis and the events that Anas and I will be discussing. You can also find two excellent pieces that Louis wrote on this subject linked in this
turns.zh: Louis 和我会讨论法国正在迅速恶化的局势、背后的推手，以及它对交易员意味着什么，还会把它和能源危机、以及我和 Anas 将谈到的那些事件联系起来。你们还能在本

turns.en: week's research, round up email, and I'm Patrick Serezna and stives straight into this interview. Anas, it's great to get you back on the show. I'm really looking forward to this. You just returned last night from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where you attended the energy week conferences there. What did you learn? What's the talk there?
turns.zh: 周的研究综述邮件里，找到 Louis 就这个主题写的两篇精彩文章。好了，让我们直接进入今天的访谈。Anas，很高兴请你回到节目里，我非常期待这次对话。你昨晚才从沙特阿拉伯利雅得回来，在那里参加了能源周系列会议。你了解到了什么？当地都在议论些什么？

turns.en: What is everybody in Riyadh see in terms of what comes next in this crisis? Thank you, Eric. The three C's crisis, when we talk about the three C's crisis, we are talking about the Gulf, we are talking about the Red Sea, and we are also talking about the Black Sea.
turns.zh: 利雅得的大家都在怎么看这场危机接下来的走向？谢谢你，Erik。所谓“三海”危机（three seas crisis），我们说的是波斯湾、红海，还有黑海。

turns.en: And this has changed energy markets and probably forever, not only energy, as we discussed in previous shows, the fertilizer industry, the agricultural trade, etc. And the three C's crisis made everyone realize just how in the interdependent, the global economy really is.
turns.zh: 这已经改变了能源市场，而且很可能是永久性的。不只是能源——就像我们在之前几期节目里讨论过的——还有化肥行业、农产品贸易等等。这场三海危机让所有人意识到，全球经济彼此依存的程度到底有多深。

turns.en: And this is, of course, one of the main lessons of those conferences or the energy week in Riyadh. The core message, basically, is summed up by Prince Ablaziz, who is the Saudi energy minister, who emphasized that global energy security cannot be taken for granted, and that an inclusive
turns.zh: 这当然是利雅得那些会议、或者说能源周的主要教训之一。核心信息基本上可以由 Abdulaziz 亲王（Prince Abdulaziz）来概括，他是沙特能源大臣，他强调全球能源安全不能被视为理所当然，而且一场包容性的

turns.en: energy transition, a reliable supply chains must be or must advance side by side. And he made the statement, I think, that is a very important statement for everyone to realize. He said, there can be no energy future for all without energy security for all, which means that, look, if Saudi Arabia is hit, everyone is going to be hit.
turns.zh: 能源转型（energy transition）和可靠的供应链必须齐头并进。他还讲了一句话，我认为是对所有人都非常重要、值得体会的。他说，没有人人共享的能源安全，就不可能有人人共享的能源未来。这话的意思是：你看，如果沙特阿拉伯遭到打击，所有人都会跟着遭殃。

turns.en: That's what the bottom line is. And that, by the way, leads me to the point, we have people on Twitter and others who are celebrating attacks on Saudi Arabia, on ships, on tankers, in the Gulf, in the Hermes straight, in the Red Sea, simply because they wanted oil prices to go up.
turns.zh: 这就是问题的关键。顺便说一句，这也让我想到：在 Twitter 等平台上，有一些人在为针对沙特阿拉伯、针对船只、针对油轮的袭击欢呼——在波斯湾、在霍尔木兹海峡（Strait of Hormuz）、在红海——仅仅因为他们希望油价上涨。

turns.en: They want their coal options, basically, to generate money. And those are no different from the merchants of death, who create wars and make money out of those wars. When we talk about the lessons out of what I learned, basically, there are several of them. We cannot discuss all of them today, but I will mention a few of them.
turns.zh: 说白了，他们就是想让自己押涨的看涨期权（call options）头寸赚钱。这些人和那些“死亡商人”（merchants of death）没什么两样——后者制造战争，再从战争中牟利。说到我从中学到的教训，其实有好几条，今天没法全部展开，但我会提其中几条。

turns.en: The first thing is the expansion of the Saudi pipelines. The Saudi pipeline east-west used to have a capacity of 5.5 million barrels a day. They expanded it to 7 million barrels a day. Now they want to expand the total pipeline capacity, not only that east-west, basically,
turns.zh: 第一件事是沙特管道的扩建。沙特那条东西向管道（East-West pipeline）原本的输送能力是每天 550 万桶，他们把它扩到了每天 700 万桶。现在他们想扩大的是管道总输送能力，而不只是那条东西向管道，

turns.en: the total capacity of Saudi Arabia that circumvent Hermes to 10 million. And what they want to do, basically, is a couple of things here. One of them is to build the pipeline through the empty quarter to Oman. So that will go directly to the Arabian Sea and to the Indian Ocean without going through
turns.zh: 而是要把沙特能够绕开霍尔木兹的管道总能力提升到每天 1000 万桶。他们想做的其实有几件事。其中之一是修一条穿过鲁卜哈利沙漠（Empty Quarter，“空旷之地”）通往阿曼（Oman）的管道，这样就能直接抵达阿拉伯海和印度洋，而不必经过

turns.en: any of the waterways, and it goes to Asia directly. So that's really the main option. They think they can finish that within two, three years if they can finish all the paperwork and do all the studies, etc. The other issue is other countries, other Gulf countries that want to pipeline or to want
turns.zh: 任何那些水道，直接通往亚洲。所以这才是主要的选项。他们认为，如果能办完所有审批文件、做完所有可行性研究等等，两三年内就能建成。另一件事是，其他海湾国家如果想要修管道、想要

turns.en: to build pipelines, they can attach to this pipeline, which means that Iraq can build pipeline from north to south to connect to this pipeline, Kuwait can do the same. So the idea here is there will be no pipelines to the Red Sea. There will be all going south to Oman, if they can, all of them basically agree to have
turns.zh: 建管道，就可以接入这条管道。也就是说，伊拉克（Iraq）可以修一条从北到南的管道接进来，科威特（Kuwait）也可以照做。所以这里的思路是：不再有通往红海的管道，而是全部向南通往阿曼——如果他们能做到的话——大家都一致同意让

turns.en: all those pipelines circumventing the Hermes straight. The other thing that Prince basically mentioned that they do have a gas pipeline east to west. And he said that they don't need the gas in certain months, they need it in the summer months. So they can within a few weeks, three, four, five weeks, they can clean it up and get
turns.zh: 所有这些管道都绕开霍尔木兹海峡。亲王还提到的另一点是，他们确实有一条东西向的天然气管道。他说，某些月份他们并不需要那条天然气管道，只有夏季月份才需要。所以他们可以在几周内——三周、四周、五周——把它清理干净、

turns.en: it ready to ship oil in it, they can add about 1.2 million barrels a day until May and then clean it up again and bring the gas again. So they have some optionality there. The other lesson I learned, which is kind of an amazing lesson, the kind of like a master class in logistics. And here is why I'm saying this.
turns.zh: 准备好用来输油，这样在 5 月之前能额外增加大约每天 120 万桶的输送量，之后再把它清理干净、重新恢复输气。所以他们在这方面有一定的灵活选择空间（optionality）。我学到的另一条教训，可以说相当惊人，简直是一堂物流调度的大师课（master class in logistics）。我这么说是因为——

turns.en: As you know, Saudi Arabia been attacked from all sides, from the Gulf, from the Red Sea, from the north, from the Iraqis and the airport was attacked. And the other airports in Jeddah and Abha and the Mam were attacked too. And now they have those conferences, they have the World Petroleum Congress with the number
turns.zh: 如你所知，沙特阿拉伯遭到了四面八方的袭击——来自波斯湾、来自红海、来自北方、来自伊拉克方向，机场也遭到了袭击。吉达（Jeddah）和艾卜哈（Abha）等其他地方的机场同样遇袭。而就在这个时候，他们要办这些会议，包括世界石油大会（World Petroleum Congress），而

turns.en: of people who registered for it, basically was record high. This is a 90 year old conference. And yet they were able to break record in terms of registration. And people from all around the world were coming in. And how to operate five conferences in one week with all this international community
turns.zh: 报名参加的人数创下了历史纪录。这是一个已经有 90 年历史的会议，可他们还是打破了报名人数的纪录，世界各地的人都在赶来。想想看，要在机场关闭、这么多国际

turns.en: coming in without an airport because they closed the airport. I was there, by the way, regarding when the airport was closed. So how to operate that? That was literally a master class in logistics. My interpretation of that is that these Saudis have long experience moving oil from east to west via that pipeline.
turns.zh: 来宾却没有机场可用的情况下——因为机场关闭了，我本人当时就在现场，正好赶上——一周内同时操办五场会议。这要怎么运作？那真的是一堂物流调度的大师课。我的解读是，沙特人长期以来积累了丰富的经验，通过那条管道把石油从东往西输送；

turns.en: And together with the annual management of the Hodge, that the pelagramid, where millions of Muslims converge on the holy cities of Makkah and Medina, within a tightly fixed window like a very fixed time a year, all of them come at once and leave at once, a million.
turns.zh: 再加上每年对朝觐（Hajj）的组织管理——数百万穆斯林在一个极其固定的时间窗口里涌向麦加（Mecca）和麦地那（Medina）这两座圣城，一年就那么一段固定时间，所有人一起来、又一起走，上百万人。

turns.en: That given the Saudis deep operational expertise in large scale logistics and their pressure. And we've seen it during this conference. I've seen it firsthand. I experienced that firsthand. So the experience basically or this expertise was shown or was on display last week.
turns.zh: 这些都让沙特人在大规模物流调度方面积累了极深的运营专长，也练就了抗压能力。我们在这次会议期间就见识到了，我亲眼所见、亲身经历。所以这种经验、这种专长，上周充分展现了出来。

turns.en: The level of organization, the level of or the ability basically to manage all those ministers to bring them in safely and send them back safely. Thousands of delegates has to be rerouted so they can still reach the events and arrangements for their eventual departure were being managed with the same precision.
turns.zh: 那种组织水平，那种把各国部长都安排妥当、安全接来又安全送回去的能力。数千名与会代表不得不临时改道，以便仍能赶到会场，而他们最终离境的安排，也以同样精准的方式被统筹着。

turns.en: So that's why it was a master class in logistics. I did arrive in Riyadh without any problems before the major attack on the airport. The airport was closed literally the day before the events began when everyone started showing up. And they were again flying from all around the world.
turns.zh: 所以说，这是一堂物流调度的大师课。我本人是在机场遭到大规模袭击之前顺利抵达利雅得的，没遇到任何问题。就在各项活动开始、大家陆续抵达的前一天，机场突然关闭了，而这些代表又是从世界各地飞来的。

turns.en: Aircrafts were diverted to other cities, to other countries. Minister were brought in private jets to nearby available airports, then driven by road to Riyadh, the speed and the flexibility with which the contingencies were handled, again demonstrated this level of logistical capability that the world can learn from.
turns.zh: 航班被迫改降到其他城市、其他国家。部长们则用私人飞机送到附近可用的机场，再由公路驱车送往利雅得。处理这些突发状况的速度和灵活性，再次展现出这种值得全世界学习的物流调度能力。

turns.en: The third point is what Secretary of Energy, US Secretary of Energy, Chris Stride, said on Hormuz flows, right basically participated virtually, but that's another issue I noticed. The capabilities of the conference basically or those five conferences to communicate remotely
turns.zh: 第三点是关于美国能源部长 Chris Wright 谈到的霍尔木兹运输流量的问题——他其实是远程连线参加的。但这又引出我注意到的另一个问题：这几场会议、或者说这五场会议远程沟通的能力。

turns.en: without any glitch, without any interruption, the pictures were very clear, the sound was very clear, was just amazing. In fact, I have never been at a conference where you have virtual speakers with this clarity. Dride basically attended a whole session and he said that 80% to 90% of pre-conflict levels
turns.zh: 没有任何卡顿、没有任何中断，画面非常清晰，声音也非常清晰，简直令人惊叹。事实上，我从没参加过哪个会议，能让远程连线的讲者达到这种清晰度。Wright 部长整整参加了一整场讨论，他说，冲突前 80% 到 90% 的

turns.en: of oil flow was going through Hormuz straight, moving about 13 to 14 million barrels a day. I know a lot of people doubt that and people think that those numbers are incorrect, etc. I and I agree that there is double counting there and we don't know what's in this oil,
turns.zh: 石油流量仍在通过霍尔木兹海峡，每天大约输送 1300 万到 1400 万桶。我知道很多人怀疑这个数字，觉得这些数字不对等等。我也同意其中存在重复计算的问题，而且我们并不清楚这些“石油”里到底包含什么——

turns.en: whether it's crude products, NGLs, etc., regardless of this it is very clear that some of those statements are made on one night basis, not over a week for example or over a month. But what was striking to me was he was able to highlight clearly that while they were able
turns.zh: 是原油、成品油，还是天然气凝析液（NGLs）等等。不管怎样，很明显，其中一些说法是基于某一个晚上的数据，而不是比如一周或一个月的。但让我印象深刻的是，他能够清楚地指出：尽管他们能够

turns.en: to move all this crude, only 25 to 35% of products of pre-crisis levels were moving in. And this is where the problem is, when we talk about the diesel crisis, that's where it is really. We are not able to recover the diesel we lost from the Gulf until today. And probably he was trying to highlight that.
turns.zh: 把所有这些原油运出去，但成品油的流量只恢复到危机前水平的 25% 到 35%。问题就出在这里——我们谈柴油危机时，真正的症结就在这儿。直到现在，我们都没能补回从波斯湾损失掉的那些柴油。他大概就是想强调这一点。

turns.en: However, what was also important to that, every single minister attended those five conferences, showed their support for Saudi Arabia, condemned the attacks on the airport, and Chris Wright basically was a little emotional when he was talking about this in his talk.
turns.zh: 不过同样重要的是，出席那五场会议的每一位部长都表达了对沙特阿拉伯的支持，谴责了对机场的袭击，而 Chris Wright 在发言中谈到这件事时，情绪也有些激动。

turns.en: One of the striking points at one of the conferences, which was the IF, the International Energy Forum conference, was a ministerial meeting that I participated in, where the economy minister of Germany, who controlled the energy thing in Germany, made a statement that was crazy statement.
turns.zh: 其中一场会议上有个令人印象深刻的点——那是国际能源论坛（International Energy Forum，IEF）的会议，我参加了一场部长级会议，德国主管能源事务的经济部长在会上发表了一番相当惊人的言论。

turns.en: And she repeated that again the following day at the World Petroleum Congress. She said that they are planning to bring back refining capacity. So she is talking about those closed refineries. They are going to open them up and bring them back online.
turns.zh: 第二天她在世界石油大会上又重复了一遍。她说，他们正计划把炼油产能重新恢复起来。她讲的是那些已经关闭的炼油厂——他们要重新开工、让它们重新投产。

turns.en: You are talking about Germany, the queen of green, who closed refineries because of climate change policies, and now under pressure because of energy security, bringing back the refineries. So the issue here is we have to see how this crisis is changing the attitude and changing policies,
turns.zh: 你说的可是德国啊，这个“绿色女王”（queen of green），当初因为气候变化政策关掉了炼油厂，如今却在能源安全的压力下，又要把这些炼油厂重新开起来。所以问题在于，我们得看看这场危机是如何改变人们的态度、改变政策的，

turns.en: which is something I will talk about later on this show. What was striking too was a statement made by the Turkish energy minister. He was talking about this massive growth in electricity demand in Turkey. And he talked of course about renewables, he talked about nuclear, etc.
turns.zh: 这一点我在本期节目后面会谈到。同样令人印象深刻的是土耳其能源部长的一番话。他谈到土耳其电力需求的巨大增长，当然也谈到了可再生能源、核能等等。

turns.en: But he made a statement that was, I never knew this by the way, this is the first time I heard of this. He said power demand or electricity demand was increasing because of AI and data centers, but he also mentioned the salination plans. We are not talking about the Gulf here, we are talking about Turkey.
turns.zh: 但他说了一句话——顺便说一句，我以前根本不知道，这是我第一次听说——他说，电力需求之所以增长，是因为 AI 和数据中心；但他还提到了海水淡化厂（desalination plants）。我们这里说的不是波斯湾，而是土耳其。

turns.en: We are talking about the country that's supposed to be rich in water. They are talking about the salination plans. And they say he said that the demand for electricity is increasing because of the increasing number of the salination plans. This is kind of the nexus of energy and water. So this was a striking issue to me.
turns.zh: 我们说的可是一个本该水资源丰富的国家，他们却在谈海水淡化厂。他说，电力需求之所以增加，正是因为海水淡化厂越来越多。这其实就是能源与水之间的纽带（nexus）。所以这一点让我印象深刻。

turns.en: The other issue is the energy transition versus energy additions. Or you can look at it as net zero versus zero energy in a sense. Saudi and OPEC speakers that include the Secretary General of OPEC, Haitham al-Rez, both of them basically the Saudis and the OPEC officials stressed energy security,
turns.zh: 另一个议题是能源转型（energy transition）与能源“增量”（energy addition）之争，或者从某种意义上说，是净零（net zero）与“零能源”之争。沙特和 OPEC 的发言人——包括 OPEC 秘书长 Haitham Al-Ghais——无论是沙特方面还是 OPEC 官员，都强调能源安全、

turns.en: reliability and the continued centrality of oil and gas. So they kept talking about oil and gas is going to stay with us for a long time. I mean Nasir who is the CEO of Aramco, Saudi Aramco, described the current situation as an energy addition, the in a fact that they are saying there is no energy transition,
turns.zh: 可靠性，以及油气持续的核心地位。他们不断强调，石油和天然气还会陪伴我们很长时间。我是说，沙特阿美（Saudi Aramco）的 CEO Amin Nasser 就把当前局面描述为一种“能源增量”——事实上他们的意思是，根本没有什么能源转型，

turns.en: there is only energy addition. And everyone agreed with him whether from OPEC or the Saudi energy ministry that oil will remain and oil and gas basically will remain the core of the energy business while new sources that include solar and wind are added. So people were emphasizing this point.
turns.zh: 只有能源增量而已。无论是 OPEC 还是沙特能源部，所有人都赞同他的说法：石油会继续存在，油气基本上仍将是能源行业的核心，而太阳能、风能等新能源只是被“添加”进来。所以大家都在强调这一点。

turns.en: The issue here when you talk about energy addition versus transition becomes important when we realize that the central message was net zero means zero energy security. So if you look at the three seas crisis, everything is about energy security here,
turns.zh: 而当我们意识到核心信息是“净零就意味着零能源安全”时，能源增量与能源转型之争就变得至关重要。所以如果你看这场三海危机，这里的一切归根结底都是能源安全问题，

turns.en: but they are still emphasizing the point that those climate change policies net zero basically means zero energy security. And we see it in Europe right now, you have those crisis in various places and all of a sudden Europe got stuck and Germany is returning back to those
turns.zh: 但他们仍在强调：那些气候变化政策、那个净零，基本上就意味着零能源安全。我们现在在欧洲就看到了这一点——各地爆发那些危机，欧洲一下子陷入困境，德国正在回到那些

turns.en: old refineries because of that energy security. But the final point is regarding my remarks at the IF meeting. I argued that the three seas crisis are accelerating the inward turn among most countries. And this is producing greater redundancy and more optionality between domestic sources
turns.zh: 老旧炼油厂，就是因为能源安全。最后一点，是关于我在 IEF 会议上发言的内容。我提出，三海危机正在加速大多数国家“向内转”的趋势。这正在带来更大的冗余度，以及国内供应源

turns.en: and imports depending on the price and cost and continued role for coal in many systems. Why I am saying this? Because when I listened to the ministers and I listened to the experts and I listened to the officials, everyone who basically was talking about resilient system that they want
turns.zh: 与进口之间更多的可选空间——视价格和成本而定，还有煤炭在许多能源体系中的持续角色。我为什么这么说？因为当我听那些部长、专家、官员发言时，几乎每个人都在谈他们想要建设的韧性系统（resilient system），

turns.en: to build resiliency and they want to diversify exports and imports. So they were talking about resiliency on one side and diversification on the other. But that does not go below the veneer. If you deep dive into it, you find out that resiliency means infrastructure redundancy
turns.zh: 想要建立韧性、想要让进出口多元化。所以他们一边谈韧性，一边谈多元化。但这只是停留在表面。如果你深入探究，就会发现韧性意味着基础设施的冗余，

turns.en: and that's costly. That means it's additional cost. And when you talk about diversification, attach to it, it means more volatility than ever because you have this optionality. So infrastructure redundancy and diversification is the name of the game now to ensure
turns.zh: 而这是有代价的，意味着额外的成本。而说到多元化，与之相伴的，是比以往任何时候都更大的波动性，因为你有了这种可选空间。所以，基础设施冗余加多元化，就是当下确保

turns.en: energy security. While the three seas crisis support additional growth, renewables, EVs, storage batteries, but they also make coal, oil, gas more entrenched. Here's the problem. None of that is incorporated in any energy markets outlook yet. This idea of optionality, for example,
turns.zh: 能源安全的关键所在（the name of the game）。三海危机一方面支撑了可再生能源、电动车、储能电池的额外增长，但另一方面也让煤炭、石油、天然气的地位更加根深蒂固。问题就在这里：这些目前都还没有被纳入任何一份能源市场展望。比如“可选空间”（optionality）这个概念——

turns.en: where you have redundancy and you have diversification, you are secured from an energy point of view. But now you look at prices and say, okay, well, now prices outside are cheaper than my domestic market. So I'm going to buy from outside. But next month, once prices go up, I'm going to cut my
turns.zh: 有了冗余、有了多元化，从能源角度看你就安全了。但这时你看看价格，说：好，现在国外价格比我国内市场便宜，那我从国外买。可下个月价格一涨，我就要削减

turns.en: imports and go to domestic sources. This type of volatility we are not used to. And it's not incorporated in any outlook. So these are some of the messages and some of the discussions from those, from those conferences. Honest, there's a huge amount to unpack there, but the thing
turns.zh: 进口、转向国内供应。这种波动是我们不习惯的，也没有被纳入任何展望。所以，这些就是那几场会议传达的部分信息和部分讨论。Anas，这里面有太多值得细细拆解的东西了，但在你的描述中最

turns.en: that really stood out to me in your description of all this and congratulations on surviving what sounds like a very difficult situation there. If they had the presence of mind, the hooties or whoever made these attacks on the airport, obviously they knew about these
turns.zh: 让我印象深刻的——还得先恭喜你平安度过了那边听上去非常凶险的局面。如果那些袭击机场的人——胡塞武装（Houthis）也好、其他人也好——真有那份心思，那他们显然是知道这些

turns.zh: 会议的。他们发动这些袭击，就是要让关键人物难以赶到会场。如果他们有这样的远见，那就意味着，一旦沙特阿拉伯及其伙伴尝试把东西向管道改道、向南通往阿曼，那么在接下来两年里，这项

turns.en: construction over the next two years unless this war is resolved fairly quickly. It means that it will be targeted and they'll do everything they can to prevent it from happening. So did the conference talk about what's its stake in terms of how promptly this conflict in Iran needs to be
turns.zh: 建设工程——除非这场战争很快得到解决——显然都会成为被攻击的目标，他们会竭尽所能阻止它建成。那么，会议上有没有谈到，这场伊朗冲突需要多快解决、这其中的利害有多大，

If it's a major construction project, it seems like that's a big risk to be interfered with by military opponents. turns.zh: 以及他们为做这些缓解措施而制定的计划面临哪些威胁？如果这是一个大型建设项目，那它似乎很容易被军事对手干扰，是个不小的风险。这个会议原本定在 4 月，早在这场冲突爆发之前，

turns.en: So in most cases, basically the focus was the traditional issues away from politics and etc. But some ministers basically have to address this in general. So the attacks, the way you mentioned it, etc. was not addressed. But I know one thing that the UAE already started building the
turns.zh: 所以大多数情况下，重点还是那些传统议题，尽量避开政治之类。但有些部长不得不泛泛地谈到这件事。所以你提到的那些袭击等等，并没有被专门讨论。不过我知道一件事：阿联酋（UAE）已经开始建设

turns.en: second pipeline despite the war. So they are doing it. And it will be very tough to waste a multi-million dollar rocket on the start of construction rather than destroying the final product. For me, it does not make sense to delay the construction one way or the other at a very high cost.
turns.zh: 第二条管道，尽管还在打仗。也就是说他们在做。而且，把一枚价值数百万美元的火箭弹浪费在刚开工的工地上、而不是用来摧毁成品，是很不划算的。在我看来，无论如何，以很高的代价去推迟这项建设都说不过去。

turns.en: Let's talk about refineries. Another subject that I've become very concerned about. You talked about people cheering the difficulty Saudi Arabia has had. I'm really disgusted by people who are cheering the destruction of refineries in Russia just because they're in
turns.zh: 我们来谈谈炼油厂。这是另一个让我非常担忧的话题。你提到有人为沙特阿拉伯遇到的困难而叫好。而我真的厌恶那些为俄罗斯炼油厂被摧毁而欢呼的人，仅仅因为它们位于

turns.en: Russia. As you know, had a problem for years before any war broke out that we didn't have enough refineries in the West to refine our products. And there is no user of crude oil other than refineries. It's the finished products that we need. So I'm concerned if we continue to make military
turns.zh: 俄罗斯。你知道，早在任何战争爆发之前很多年，我们就存在一个问题：西方没有足够的炼油厂来把油品炼出来。而除了炼油厂，原油没有其他使用者，我们真正需要的是成品油。所以我很担心，如果我们继续把炼油厂变成军事

turns.en: targets out of refineries. People are cheering it. We're getting rid of Russian refineries. Wait a minute. It means the whole world is going to have a crack spread explosion problem that I don't think can be solved until you build new refineries. Now, maybe I'm misunderstanding
turns.zh: 打击目标——人们还在为此欢呼，“我们在消灭俄罗斯的炼油厂”。且慢，这意味着全世界都将面临裂解价差（crack spread）暴涨的问题，而我认为，除非新建炼油厂，否则这个问题根本无解。当然，也许是我误解了

turns.en: the news and it's just a matter of a repair bill to fix these refineries that are being attacked. But based on the video I've been seeing, it looks like some of them are being destroyed. And usually it takes 10 years to build a new refinery from scratch. We don't have the ability in
turns.zh: 新闻，也许这些遇袭的炼油厂只是需要一笔维修费就能修好。但从我看到的视频来看，其中一些似乎是被彻底摧毁了。而通常，从零开始建一座新炼油厂需要 10 年。全球经济可承受不起

turns.en: the global economy to suffer 10 years that we don't have the ability to refine crude oil. So am I exaggerating to think the problem with refineries is that bad? And if not, why not? No, you are spot on Eric. And in fact, we'd be writing about this in our report for months.
turns.zh: 连续 10 年没有能力炼化原油的局面。所以，我把炼油厂的问题想得这么严重，是夸张了吗？如果不是，那为什么不是？不，你说得完全在理，Erik。事实上，这个问题我们在报告里已经写了好几个月了。

turns.en: And we've been, by the way, we've been attacked on social media for saying that. We are apolitical when we talk about or analyzing the market. Yet it was very clear that attacking the Russia refineries is going to hurt people around the world and is going to hurt farmers in
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，我们还因为这么讲而在社交媒体上遭到攻击。我们在谈论或分析市场时是不带政治立场的。但很显然，袭击俄罗斯的炼油厂会伤害全世界的人，会伤害

turns.en: Africa and South America and other places and is going to affect the livelihood of people in Egypt and Kenya and other places. So that was very clear. So you are spot on on this. The issue here is we lost many refineries in the United States mostly in California.
turns.zh: 非洲、南美洲和其他地方的农民，还会影响埃及、肯尼亚等地民众的生计。这一点非常清楚。所以你说得完全对。问题在于，我们在美国损失了很多炼油厂，主要是在加利福尼亚州（California）；

turns.en: We lost many refineries in Europe like I mentioned earlier in Germany. And now we are seeing the Russian refineries being hit. The Saudi refineries being hit. Before that during the war, the active war or the big war, whatever you want to call it, in March and April,
turns.zh: 在欧洲也损失了很多炼油厂，就像我前面提到的德国。现在我们又看到俄罗斯的炼油厂被打击、沙特的炼油厂被打击。在那之前，在这场战争——或者说全面战争、大战，随你怎么叫——的 3 月和 4 月期间，

turns.zh: 阿联酋的鲁韦斯（Ruwais）炼油厂遭到了打击。所以我们损失惨重。而之所以爆发柴油危机，是因为我们损失了波斯湾那些炼油厂的油品，接着又出现了恐慌，导致各国禁止成品油出口；然后还有船只改道，把更多

turns.zh: 成品油漂在海上、而不是运抵目的地。交易商还在囤积，然后就是黑海的问题。人们并没有意识到发生了什么。媒体在其中扮演了非常恶劣的角色。因为整整一周——我记得很清楚——

turns.en: Yet the media got fixated with it. At the time when we lost 3 million barrels, a day of crude. And we lost 800,000 barrels of diesel in the black sea. And the media ignored that completely. For months, the media refused to talk about what's happening in the black sea.
turns.zh: 可媒体却盯着它不放。而就在那段时间，我们每天损失了 300 万桶原油，在黑海损失了 80 万桶柴油，媒体却对此完全无视。好几个月里，媒体拒绝谈论黑海正在发生的事。

turns.en: They told us about the oil spills in the Gulf and near Oman, and they ignored all the oil spills in the black sea. If it wasn't for present from basically bringing up the issue a month ago, and accusing Zelinsky for the diesel shortages, etc., the media would have ignored it completely.
turns.zh: 他们向我们报道波斯湾和阿曼附近的漏油事件，却对黑海所有的漏油只字不提。要不是普京（Putin）大约一个月前把这个问题提出来、指责 Zelensky 造成了柴油短缺等等，媒体本来会完全无视它。

turns.en: So I'm glad to see the media talking about the black sea today. It is a serious problem. And whatever happens in the Gulf, we have to remember that this three seas crisis that we have is multi-dimensional, multi-level, multi-commodity affecting everyone in the world.
turns.zh: 所以我很高兴今天看到媒体开始谈论黑海了。这是个严重的问题。而且无论波斯湾发生什么，我们都必须记住，我们面对的这场三海危机是多维度、多层次、多商品的，影响着世界上的每一个人。
